title: Exceptions
bridge: `try { } catch (FormatException e) { } finally { }`; throw your own with `throw new ArgumentException("why");`. For input, prefer `TryParse`, which avoids exceptions entirely.

exercises.title: Safe number
exercises.prompt: Write ToNumber(string text) in class SafeNum returning a double? (a double or null): the number for "42", "2.5", "2,5" or " 7 ", null for anything else. Use double.TryParse with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture.
hints: double.TryParse(s, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out double v) ? v : null

exercises.title: Refuse bad input
exercises.prompt: Write PricePerKg(double total, double kg) in class PerKg: total / kg rounded to 2 decimals; throw ArgumentException if kg <= 0 or total < 0.
hints: if (kg <= 0 || total < 0) throw new ArgumentException("bad input");

quiz.why: Using something that's null, like a component that was never assigned.

quiz.q: Cleanest way to read a number someone typed?

cards.q: Name of a parameter as text?

explain: Explain exceptions to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
